props.statement: Water gas (about 50-65% CO, 30-45% hydrogen) is passed at 50 to 150 atmospheres through a chain of reaction vessels in series: pure zinc oxide in the first vessel or vessels, a methanol catalyst containing copper or manganese (e.g. copper oxide and zinc oxide) in the rest, at the temperatures usual for each catalyst, usually 200° to 540° C. and particularly 300° to 450° C.; methanol is removed between vessels by cooling and/or water scrubbing and the gas reheated; four or five vessels usually convert substantially all the gas.
